newsitem.title: INDIA: India, Pakistan to set dates next month for talks.
newsitem.headline: India, Pakistan to set dates next month for talks.

text.p: India and Pakistan have put off bilateral talks between their highest-ranking diplomats until after their prime ministers meet in May, an Indian Foreign Ministry spokesman said on Tuesday.
"We hope to establish mutually convenient dates in the near future. Most probably this will be done in the meeting of the prime ministers in Male in May," the spokesman told a news conference.
The foreign secretaries of the two countries held talks in New Delhi in March after a three-year break and are scheduled to meet again.
Indian and Pakistani officials had earlier said they hoped the diplomats could meet in Islamabad in the first week of May.
"There were certain suggestions from the Pakistani side. However, for logistical reasons, they could not be accepted," the Foreign Ministry spokesman said.
Indian Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral is due to hold discussions with his Pakistani counterpart, Nawaz Sharif, on the sidelines of a regional summit in the Maldives between May 12 and 14.
Gujral said on Saturday he expected to identify several areas of cooperation with Pakistan at the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation summit in Male.
Any headway in technical areas would likely have to be made in discussions between the foreign secretaries.
Official talks resumed this year after discussions were derailed in 1994 over Kashmir. India controls two thirds of Kashmir and the Pakistan the rest, but both countries claim the entire region.
India and Pakistan have gone to war three times over the past 50 years, twice over Kashmir.
